scenes.text: You've got running water. But where does it go after it goes down the drain?
Gravity again. Every drain pipe tilts slightly downhill, so the water always flows away from your house.
Little pipes join bigger pipes, called sewers. And they all flow to the lowest spot in town.
Step one. A big metal screen catches all the junk. Wipes, toys, even hair.
Next, a giant still tank. Heavy gunk sinks to the bottom. Grease floats to the top. Both get scraped off.
Then you pump in air, and trillions of tiny bacteria eat the dirt that's left.
What comes out is clean enough to flow back into the river.
Which flows into the lake. The same lake your tap water came from.
So whatever you do, never flush wipes.
